metadata.status_reason: Re-onboarded 2026-08-28 onto HarvardJournalsMultisiteAdapter. journals.law.harvard.edu is a WordPress Multisite install; the shared WordPressAcademicBaseAdapter rooted REST/sitemap at the bare origin (network root has zero posts) and, with a /lpr/hlprvolumes/ seed prefix, could not reach the issue pages, which live at /lpr/volume-N-M/ and /lpr/print-archive/volume-N-M/. No PDFs were produced. Issue pages have no per-article HTML pages, so titles fall back to the issue page title - fix downstream with first-page PDF metadata extraction.
metadata.status_evidence_ref: smoke 2026-08-28: /lpr/hlprvolumes/ -> 39 issue links (Vol 1 No 1 2007 .. Vol 20 No 1 2026), issue pages carry 8-12 PDFs each, all under /lpr/; PDF GET 200 application/pdf

publication_scope.notes: Discovery, traversal and PDF acceptance are gated on the /lpr/ path prefix, including PDFs under /lpr/wp-content/uploads/sites/89/. Other Harvard journals on this host are out of scope.

navigation.pagination: none - one page lists all 39 issues
navigation.notes: Issue-page URLs are inconsistent across eras: /lpr/volume-20-1/, /lpr/hlprvolumes/volume-19-1/, /lpr/print-archive/volume-9-2/, /lpr/print-archive-volume-12-1/. Volume 16 Number 2 is linked as a bare whole-issue PDF with no issue page. Issue pages mix article PDFs with front matter, mastheads and whole-volume files - split/classify downstream. HTML-first discovery: the journal's Jetpack sitemap (/lpr/sitemap.xml, 692 URLs) and REST API (589 posts) enumerate the whole subsite including /lpr/online-articles/ (HLPR Online) and blog posts whose bodies link third-party citation PDFs (supremecourt.gov, govinfo.gov), so they stay fallback-only. robots.txt allows these paths, Crawl-delay: 10.
